title: Guarded by God, we fear no demon
source_text: Οὐδὲ γὰρ. κἂν μὴ ὦσιν αὐτοῖς εὐμενεῖς οἱ δαίμονες, πάσχειν ἄν τι ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν δύναιντο. φρουρούμενοι ὑπὸ τοῦ εὐμενοῦς αὐτοῖς διὰ τὴν εὐσέβειαν ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς θείους αὐτοῦ ἀγγέλους ἐφιστάντος τοῖς ἀξίοις τοῦ φρουρεῖσθαι. ἵνα μηδὲν πάσχωσιν ἀπὸ τῶν δαιμόνων. ὁ δ᾿ ἔχων τὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεὸν διὰ τὴν εἰς αὐτὸν εὐσέβειαν εὐμενῆ καὶ διὰ τὸ τὸν τῆς „μεγάλης βουλῆς“ ἄγγελον τοῦ θεοῦ παραδεδέχθαι κύριον Ἰησοῦν, ἀρκούμενος τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ εὐμενείᾳ λέγοι ἂν θαῤῥῶν ὡς οὐδὲν πεισόμενος ἀπὸ παντὸς τοῦ τῶν δαιμόνων στρατοπέδου· „κύριος φωτισμός μου καὶ σωτήρ μου, τίνα φοβηθήσομαι; κύριος ὑπερασπιστὴς τῆς ζωῆς μου. ἀπὸ τίνος δειλιάσω;“ ἐρεῖ δὲ καὶ τό· „ἐὰν παρατάξηται ἐπ᾿ ἐμὲ παρεμβολὴ, οὐ φοβηθήσεται ἡ καρδία μου.“ τοσαῦτα καὶ εἰς τὸ εἰ δ᾿ εἰσί τινες δαίμονες. δηλονότι καὶ οὗτοι τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσι (ν. οἷς) καὶ πιστευτέον καὶ καλλιερητέον κατὰ νόμους καὶ προσευκτέον. ἵν᾿ εὐμενεῖς ὦσιν.
pass_a_gloss: For even if the demons are not well-disposed (εὐμενεῖς) to them, they could not suffer (πάσχειν) anything from them, being guarded (φρουρούμενοι) by the God over all, well-disposed to them through piety (εὐσέβεια), and setting (ἐφιστάντος) His divine angels over those worthy of being guarded, that they suffer nothing from the demons. And he who has the God over all well-disposed through piety toward Him, and through having received (παραδεδέχθαι) the angel of God 'of great counsel (μεγάλη βουλή)', the Lord Jesus, content (ἀρκούμενος) with the goodwill (εὐμένεια) of God through Christ Jesus, would say boldly (θαρρῶν) as one who will suffer nothing from the whole camp (στρατόπεδον) of the demons: 'The Lord is my illumination (φωτισμός) and my savior (σωτήρ), whom shall I fear? The Lord is protector (ὑπερασπιστής) of my life, of whom shall I be timid (δειλιάσω)?' And he will say also: 'If an encampment (παρεμβολή) be drawn up in battle (παρατάξηται) against me, my heart shall not fear.' So much also against: 'but if there are certain demons, clearly these too are of God, whom one must both trust and sacrifice to with good omens according to laws and pray to, that they be well-disposed.'
pass_b_english: For even if the demons are not well disposed toward them, they could suffer nothing from them, since they are guarded by the God over all, who is well disposed toward them because of their piety, and who sets His divine angels over those worthy of being guarded, so that they suffer nothing from the demons. He who has the God over all well disposed toward him through his piety toward Him, and through having received the Lord Jesus, God’s Angel “of Great Counsel” (Isaiah 9:6), and who is content with the goodwill of God through Christ Jesus, could say with confidence, as one who will suffer nothing from the whole army of demons: “The Lord is my light and my Savior; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the defender of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?” (Psalm 27:1). And he will also say: “If an army is drawn up against me, my heart will not fear” (Psalm 27:3).

So much, then, in answer to the words: “But if there are certain demons, clearly these too belong to God, and we must trust them, and offer acceptable sacrifices to them according to the laws, and pray to them, so that they may be well disposed.”

choices.choice: ‘Angel of Great Counsel’ is the LXX title in Isaiah 9:6 (LXX 9:5, μεγάλης βουλῆς ἄγγελος), read by Origen of Christ; capitalised as a title of Christ. Origen’s phrase τὸν τῆς μεγάλης βουλῆς ἄγγελον τοῦ θεοῦ ... κύριον Ἰησοῦν is rendered ‘the Lord Jesus, God’s Angel of Great Counsel’, without repeating ‘Angel’. ἀρκούμενος is a participle under the same subject as λέγοι ἄν, so ‘who is content ... could say’ keeps one sentence. Psalms quoted from LXX Psalm 26:1 and 26:3, which are Psalm 27:1 and 27:3 in English Bibles; Origen’s wording matches the LXX (‘my light and my Savior’, ‘defender of my life’, παρατάξηται ἐπ᾿ ἐμὲ παρεμβολή). ‘Sets His divine angels over those worthy of being guarded’ may echo Psalm 91:11 (LXX 90:11) or Psalm 34:7 (LXX 33:8); no verbal match, so left uncited. In the closing repetition of Celsus’s words the transmitted text has εἰσι(ν. οἷς), an editorial restoration of οἷς (‘whom’) from chapter 24; translated as in chapter 24.
'the Angel "of Great Counsel", the Angel of God, the Lord Jesus' (doubled 'Angel', not in the Greek) to 'the Lord Jesus, God's Angel "of Great Counsel"'
'is content with the goodwill ... He could say' (split the participle off as a main clause) to one sentence: 'and who is content with ... could say' (ἀρκούμενος under λέγοι ἄν)
Psalm 27:3 'Though an army set itself in array against me, my heart shall not fear' (archaic) to 'If an army is drawn up against me, my heart will not fear' (ἐάν + subjunctive)
'So much on the words' to 'So much, then, in answer to the words' (τοσαῦτα καὶ εἰς τό)
Checked LXX Psalm 26:1, 26:3 = Psalm 27:1, 27:3; LXX Isaiah 9:5 = Isaiah 9:6

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; the English is from the Greek.
